name: Esarhaddon
title: Assyrian king and conqueror of Egypt
summary: Esarhaddon was king of Assyria and the son of Sennacherib. He is known in the Bible for resettling foreign peoples in Samaria after the fall of Israel, and for his campaign against Egypt. He is mentioned in connection with the murder of his father Sennacherib and as a powerful Assyrian ruler during the period of the divided kingdom.

keyEvents.title: The Murder of Sennacherib
keyEvents.description: Esarhaddon's father Sennacherib was killed by his own sons Adrammelech and Sarsechim while he was worshiping in the temple of his god. Esarhaddon then succeeded him as king of Assyria.

keyEvents.title: Esarhaddon Becomes King
keyEvents.description: After the murder of Sennacherib, the murderers fled to the land of Ararat, and Esarhaddon was installed as the new king over the Assyrian empire.

keyEvents.title: Resettlement of Foreign Peoples in Samaria
keyEvents.description: Under the Assyrian Empire's policy of forced deportations, people from various nations were settled in Samaria. Esarhaddon continued this policy that his predecessors had started.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to the Rebuilding of the Temple
keyEvents.description: The peoples who had been settled in Samaria under Esarhaddon later tried to prevent the Jews from rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Assyrian Dominance over Judah
keyEvents.description: During Esarhaddon's reign, Judah under King Manasseh was a vassal state of Assyria. According to tradition, Manasseh was taken as a captive to Babylon by the Assyrian king.
